bull.b: FDA agreement on primary and secondary endpoints and an enrichment strategy meaningfully reduces late-stage regulatory design risk. This alignment strengthens the credibility of the planned registrational pathway, increasing the chance Phase 2b will inform a focused, efficient Phase 3 program and limit costly redesigns.

The absence of FDA objections after a protocol amendment and safety review de-risks clinical development by reducing the probability of a regulatory hold. It supports continued dosing across indications and validates the company's safety assessments, enabling multi-indication development planning to continue.

The ~$15M private placement materially extends operating runway into H2 2027, providing capital to execute planned Phase 1b and IND-enabling work. This reduces immediate financing pressure, allowing the company to advance clinical milestones that can unlock future partnerships or non-dilutive funding.

bear.b: Sustained operating and free cash flow burn of roughly $21M TTM creates structural dependence on external financing. Even with some improvement versus prior years, recurring negative cash generation necessitates periodic raises, which can delay programs if funding is not secured and increases long-term execution risk.

Negative shareholders' equity signals a shrinking asset base and reduced financial flexibility. This weakens borrowing capacity, can raise covenant and counterparty concerns, and increases reliance on dilutive equity or onerous financing terms to support development activities absent revenue or partnerships.

Amended loan conversion rights and repriced/added warrants increase potential future dilution and concentrate ownership dynamics. Such structural financing terms can depress shareholder value, complicate future equity raises, and materially alter capitalization if conversions or warrant exercises occur to fund operations.
